rationale: hammernik_2017-claude-agentic: vn_T=4, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=9, vn_n_bumps=51, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_filter_init_std=0.05, vn_rbf_init_std=0.01, vn_lambda_init=0.02, epochs=16, batch_size=2, lr=0.00096, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, max_train_s=1450, rationale=iter-13 (six-box; RESCOPED T=5->T=4 after OOM). First attempt (T=5, n_bumps=51) OOMed on 16GB RTX5000 in the _rho_prime bump loop (like the earlier f=24 OOM) -> 51 bumps at T=5x512px is memory-infeasible on the default pool. Test the activation-resolution hypothesis at the memory-safe T=4 base (iter-5: T=4,f=16,n_bumps=31, hr=0.6174). ONE KNOB vs iter-5: vn_n_bumps 31 -> 51 (denser RBF grid over [-2,2] -> finer learned nonlinearity rho'). HYPOTHESIS: a sharper activation improves streak/anatomy separation, lifting hr above iter-5's 0.6174; if it ties/regresses, 31 bumps already suffices. All else = iter-5 (T=4, f=16, k=9, x_range=2.0, lambda=0.02, lr=9.6e-4, batch=2, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, train_n=400). BUDGET: 51 bumps at T=4 ~ still heavier RBF loop; epochs=16 DEPENDENT budget var, max_train_s=1450 guards under the 1800s kill. batch_size=2 (OOM guard); expandable_segments via --export. NOTE: T=4x51-bump memory ~ iter-5(T=4x31)x1.65 loop but T=4<T=5 activation tensors -> expected to fit; if it OOMs again, n_bumps axis is memory-bounded and I will file that + move on.
